title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's own mathematics. It is page 72 of a typed English translation, with hand-inserted formulas, of a Russian text; the margin gives the original page reference 'p. 208'. It sits in the dossier between two manuscript pages in French on motivic Galois groups and polarisations, so it looks misfiled or used as scrap.

Setting: V is a smooth projective variety (probably a surface). E is an effective divisor and [E] its line bundle. φ = {φ_i} is a section of [E] whose zero divisor is ℰ_φ.

First step (stabilisation of H^1). Since ℰ_φ is linearly equivalent to E, O_V(-ℰ_φ)⊗[nE] ≅ O_V[(n-1)E]. Twist the sequence 0 → O_V(-ℰ_φ) → O_V → O_{ℰ_φ} → 0 by [nE]. Using a previous result (14), presumably H^1(ℰ_φ, O[nE]|ℰ_φ) = 0 for n ≥ n', one gets that dim H^1(V, O[nE]) is non-increasing in n. A non-increasing sequence of nonnegative integers is eventually constant, so for n ≥ n'' we have dim H^1(O[nE]) = dim H^1(O[(n-1)E]). This is (15).

Second step (base-point freeness). φ^n is a section of [nE], so the base locus of |nE| lies on ℰ_φ. To show there are no base points on ℰ_φ for n ≥ n_ℰ, the text introduces the restriction sequence (16). Once H^1 stabilises, the restriction H^0(V, [nE]) → H^0(ℰ_φ, [nE]|ℰ_φ) becomes surjective, and the sections on ℰ_φ are then shown to have no common zeros.

This is the classical Zariski-type argument (Zariski 1962, on Riemann–Roch for high multiples of an effective divisor and the base locus of |nE|). It is the kind of argument found in the Shafarevich-seminar volume 'Algebraic Surfaces' (Trudy MIAN 75, 1965), though the exact source is unsure.
errors: As printed, (15) does not follow immediately from the twisted exact sequence. Combined with the vanishing in (14), that sequence only gives the inequality dim H^1(O[nE]) ≤ dim H^1(O[(n-1)E]). Equality for n ≥ n'' comes from monotonicity plus the fact that the dimensions are nonnegative integers. The text compresses this step ('having taken n'' ≥ n'').
Minor translation infelicities ('there is no common zeros', 'cross-section of the group'). There are no mathematical errors visible.

ideas.what: Stabilisation of h^1(nE) via the restriction sequence to a member of |E|, and the resulting base-point freeness of |nE| for large n
ideas.modern_name: Zariski's theorem on the base locus of |nD| / semi-ampleness argument for effective divisors
ideas.usually_credited_to: O. Zariski (1962); expositions in the Shafarevich seminar 'Algebraic Surfaces' (1965)
ideas.where_published: Not Grothendieck's; this is a translation of a Russian text (original p. 208)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typed English translation of a standard Russian exposition of Zariski's base-point argument, misplaced in a motives dossier. It contains no Grothendieck content. The only mildly interesting point is archival: a foreign text on surfaces was filed among the 1965 motivic Galois notes.
transcription_corrections: The handwritten symbols the transcription renders as 'ℰ_m' (e.g. 'on ℰ_m', 'P ∉ ℰ_m') are sloppy forms of ℰ_φ, the zero divisor of φ.
The section φ^n is typed like a stylised 'm' in the image; reading it as φ^n = {φ_i^n} (φ_1^n in the typescript) is correct.
The marginal number '185' at bottom left is the archive foliation; '72' at top right is the typescript page number.
